books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: W. E. B. Du Bois, The Souls of Black Folk (1903), Chapter 2, “Of the Dawn of Freedom”

stimulus.text:
“The problem of the twentieth century is the problem of the color-line,—the relation of the darker to the lighter races of men in Asia and Africa, in America and the islands of the sea. It was a phase of this problem that caused the Civil War; and however much they who marched South and North in 1861 may have fixed on the technical points, of union and local autonomy as a shibboleth, all nevertheless knew, as we know, that the question of Negro slavery was the real cause of the conflict.”

—W. E. B. Du Bois, The Souls of Black Folk (1903), Chapter 2, “Of the Dawn of Freedom”
stimulus.source_note: W. E. B. Du Bois, The Souls of Black Folk (1903), Chapter 2, “Of the Dawn of Freedom.” Public domain (Project Gutenberg eBook #408). Wording verified against the Gutenberg text.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Du Bois wrote in 1903, a generation after Reconstruction ended. His judgment in this passage best supports which of the following conclusions about Reconstruction?

options.text: It had ended racial inequality in the United States.
options.misconception: Du Bois names the color-line as the century’s problem, so inequality endured.

options.text: It had failed because Black Southerners refused to work.
options.misconception: Du Bois blames no such thing; his chapter blames the nation’s failure to protect freedpeople.

options.text: It had been forgotten by everyone who lived through it.
options.misconception: Du Bois is writing about it in 1903 precisely because it was not forgotten.

options.text: It had left the central question of Black freedom unresolved.

rationales.A: Du Bois names the color-line as the century’s problem, so inequality endured.
rationales.B: Du Bois blames no such thing; his chapter blames the nation’s failure to protect freedpeople.
rationales.C: Du Bois is writing about it in 1903 precisely because it was not forgotten.
rationales.D: Writing nearly thirty years after 1877, Du Bois still calls race the problem of the century. If Reconstruction had settled the question, there would be no color-line left to name, but the line was still there.
rationales.general:
1. Count the years: Du Bois writes in 1903, a full generation after the troops left in 1877.
2. He still calls the color-line the problem of the century he is living in.
3. A problem that still defines a century was not solved by the generation before it.
4. Reconstruction changed the law, but the line between Black and white still shaped daily life.
Remember: a later writer’s verdict is evidence too, and Du Bois’s verdict is that the work was unfinished.
